function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have real‑time access to current weather data. You can quickly check the temperature in Riga by looking at a weather app, visiting a site like Weather.com, or searching “Riga weather” in your browser. If you’d like, I can help you set up a quick script that pulls the latest temperature from a public API.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How hot is it now in Riga?" They want current temperature. We need to provide weather info. We don't have direct access to real-time data. We can either say we can't fetch real-time data or we can approximate. But best practice: we should say we cannot fetch real-time data. We can suggest using a weather API or website. We can also ask if they'd like me to look up approximate. But we can't. So respond politely.
